nativePaths.instructionBodyTemplate:
# Hermes Agent

You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research. Be helpful, knowledgeable, direct, targeted, and efficient. Admit uncertainty when appropriate and prioritize genuine usefulness.

{{globalPolicy}}
<!-- agenthub:managed -->
nativePaths.instructionBodyTemplateSource: preamble recovered verbatim from `git show fc1bda6:templates/HERMES-SOUL.md` (header, blank, persona paragraph, blank, {{globalPolicy}} placeholder); the trailing `<!-- agenthub:managed -->` marker line was appended by Task 2 (not present in the recovered template, which predates the marker convention) to encode marker placement in data instead of special-casing it in the renderer, per the fix-round-1 coordinator instruction.
nativePaths.pluginsDirNote: Verified 2026-08-05 against hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/plugins and .../windows-native. Hermes discovers plugins from three sources: bundled (<repo>/plugins/), project (.hermes/plugins/) and user (~/.hermes/plugins/). The Windows installer sets HERMES_HOME=%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes and ~/.hermes resolves to that root, so the user path on native Windows is %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/plugins. Derived from a documented env-var mapping rather than assumed from the sibling directory names, and HERMES_HOME is overridable, so this resolves correctly only for a default install. Path correct; absent only because no personal plugin is installed.
nativePaths.configNote: Verified 2026-08-11 against hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/windows-native, which states HERMES_HOME on native Windows is %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes and lists config.yaml among the files kept there ('config.yaml, .env, skills/, sessions/, logs/, ...') because they survive reinstalls. Path correct. Absent because HERMES IS NOT INSTALLED on this host: the declared executable .../hermes-agent/venv/Scripts/hermes.exe does not exist, the hermes-agent/ install directory is missing entirely, and hermes is not on PATH. config.yaml is written by the first-run setup wizard, which has therefore never run. The only contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes are SOUL.md and skills/, both written by agenthub's own sync -- so this root exists because we created it, not because Hermes did, and the other three hermes notes below inherit that finding. Default profile only: per .../docs/user-guide/profiles, `hermes profile create <name>` sets HERMES_HOME to %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/profiles/<name>, moving config.yaml, memories/ and sessions/ with it.
nativePaths.hooksDirNote: Verified 2026-08-11 against .../docs/user-guide/features/hooks: gateway hooks live in ~/.hermes/hooks/, one subdirectory each carrying HOOK.yaml and handler.py, scanned by HookRegistry.discover_and_load() at gateway startup. ~/.hermes resolves to %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes on native Windows (see configNote), so the declared Windows form is correct. The docs describe the user creating this directory when adding a hook and never say Hermes creates it, so absence is the documented default state -- this one would be absent even on a working install, independently of the not-installed finding in configNote. Distinct from ~/.hermes/agent-hooks/, which the same page gives as the by-convention location for SHELL hook scripts registered through config.yaml; agenthub declares no path for those and should not conflate them.
nativePaths.memoriesDirNote: Verified 2026-08-11 against .../docs/user-guide/features/memory: 'Both are stored in ~/.hermes/memories/ and are injected into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot at session start.' Path correct in its Windows form (see configNote for the ~/.hermes to %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes mapping). Agent-managed -- Hermes writes it through its own memory tool -- and the docs do NOT state whether it is created eagerly at first run or lazily on first write, so creation timing is unestablished; either way it cannot exist here, because Hermes is not installed. Per-profile like config.yaml: a named profile puts memories under %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/profiles/<name>/memories. The same docs warn against pointing two agent processes at one Hermes home, because automatic memory writes from both compound into state neither authored -- worth honouring before anything is ever synced into this path.
nativePaths.sessionsDirNote: Verified 2026-08-11 against .../docs/user-guide/windows-native, which lists sessions/ among the HERMES_HOME contents that survive reinstalls. Path correct. Created when sessions are used, so it would be absent on a clean install regardless; here it is absent because Hermes is not installed at all (see configNote). Per-profile: a named profile puts sessions under %LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/profiles/<name>/sessions. agenthub declares no path for the sibling logs/ directory the same list documents, which is a deliberate omission rather than an oversight -- nothing in this repository writes or reads Hermes logs.

Flagged conflict, recorded because it would otherwise be rediscovered as a bug: cline.bot/blog/cline-v3-36-hooks describes a DIFFERENT and older hooks system belonging to the VSCode extension, rooted at ~/Documents/Cline/Rules/Hooks/ with project .clinerules/hooks/, and states it is macOS and Linux only with no Windows support. Two systems share one feature name. If a VSCode Cline host is ever registered separately, it must not reuse this path.
nativePaths.agentsDirNote: Set to null 2026-08-05: NOT ESTABLISHED, which is different from absent. Previously asserted ~/.cline/agents. Research found two conflations and no resolution. (a) The shipped subagents feature (docs.cline.bot/features/subagents) is a built-in automatic use_subagents tool with no user-authored file or directory at all -- toggled in Settings, never defined on disk. (b) The custom multi-agent 'Agent Teams' feature, which would need a directory, is documented inconsistently by Cline itself: docs.cline.bot/getting-started/config shows 'agents/  # Global agent definitions' under ~/.cline/, while docs.cline.bot/cli/cli-reference shows definitions in a project-level file .cline/agents.yaml with no global equivalent, and docs.cline.bot/cli/agent-teams documents only runtime team STATE at ~/.cline/data/teams/[team-name]/, never where definitions are authored. Two official pages disagree on whether a global path exists. Resolve by installing an Agent Team and observing where Cline writes, not by picking the page that reads more confidently.

nativePaths.instructionsNote: Added 2026-08-04 from docs.qoder.com/cli/using-cli, Memory section (subject confirmed: memory and context files, not MCP or plugins). Qoder CLI documents a three-tier hierarchy whose user level is ~/.qoder/AGENTS.md, explicitly applying to all projects. The Windows form is inferred from this host's existing configHome, which already resolves ~/.qoder to that directory and demonstrably exists. Distinct from .qoder/rules, which is project-scoped only. HTML-comment survival is not vendor-documented; the agenthub:managed marker is standard Markdown and inert in prompt context.
nativePaths.agentsDirNote: Verified 2026-08-11 against docs.qoder.com/en/cli/subagent: subagent configuration is saved to the user-level path ~/.qoder/agents/<agentName>.md, and project-level subagents take precedence over user-level ones when names collide. Path correct. Created when the first user-level subagent is generated, so absence is the documented default state. Absent for a second and more serious reason that the other two qoder notes inherit: QODER IS NOT INSTALLED on this host. The declared executable ~/.qoder/bin/qodercli/qodercli.exe does not exist and ~/.qoder/bin is missing, while an orphaned wrapper still on PATH at ~/bin/qodercli.cmd points at that exact path and fails with 'The system cannot find the path specified.' The declared path is right and the product is gone -- the wrapper's survival is what makes `qodercli` look installed. The only contents of ~/.qoder are settings.json and skills/, both written by agenthub's own sync.
nativePaths.pluginsDirNote: COULD NOT ESTABLISH from official docs, checked 2026-08-11. docs.qoder.com/cli/plugins documents installation via `qodercli plugins install`, and names ~/.qoder/, ~/.qoder/commands/ and ~/.qoder/skills/, but never states where an installed plugin lands on disk and names no marketplace or cache directory. ~/.qoder/plugins is therefore INFERRED from the sibling directory names -- precisely the inference hermes.pluginsDirNote deliberately refused, deriving its path from a documented HERMES_HOME mapping instead. Treat as unverified: do not sync into it, and do not read its absence as evidence in either direction. It cannot be settled by observation here because Qoder is not installed (see agentsDirNote); settling it needs a host with Qoder present and a plugin actually installed through the CLI, then this note replaced with that finding.
nativePaths.canvasDirNote: Probably WRONG, checked 2026-08-11 -- recorded as a correction rather than as a gap, because the two are different findings and only one of them is someone's next task. docs.qoder.com places Canvas under Desktop > Extensions, making it a Desktop application feature rather than a CLI one, and describes /canvas as producing a .canvas.tsx file rendered in a Canvas preview: a project artifact, not user-level state. No Qoder page names a ~/.qoder/canvas directory, and none of the pages that do enumerate ~/.qoder contents (using-cli, plugins, subagent) list it. So unlike pluginsDir this is not merely unverified -- the documented design points away from a user-level canvas directory existing at all. Kept rather than deleted, because deleting a declared path on the mistaken basis that a directory absent from disk must be wrong is the exact error gemini.agentsDirNote exists to record. A host with Qoder Desktop installed can settle it by observation; replace this note with that.

nativePaths.instructionsNote: Researched 2026-08-04 against docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/rules and re-checked the same day against docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/configuration (subjects confirmed: Rules/AGENTS.md and CLI configuration). Devin CLI loads a global AGENTS.md at the start of every session. The configuration page states the user config file is %APPDATA%/devin/config.json on Windows -- matching nativePaths.config here -- and instructs the reader to place AGENTS.md 'in this directory', i.e. the same user config directory, giving ~/.config/devin/AGENTS.md on Unix. The Windows form therefore derives from a documented directory rather than a guess, but the vendor never writes the Windows path literally, so this stays unresolved rather than being promoted to a deployment target. The separate Devin cloud Knowledge feature is an account setting, not a local file.
nativePaths.mcpNote: Verified 2026-08-04. docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/mcp documents only PROJECT scope (.devin/mcp_config.json and .devin/mcp_config.local.json, key mcpServers) and says nothing about user-level MCP -- which nearly became a false finding that Sync-AgentHub.ps1 writes MCP where Devin does not read it. Checking the live file settled it: %APPDATA%/devin/config.json already carries an mcpServers object with six Devin-owned entries (context7, descript, exa, firecrawl, linear, notion) that AgentHub never wrote. The global key is real and the vendor page is merely incomplete. Sync-AgentHub.ps1's ProtectKeys behavior exists to keep those host-owned entries from being pruned.
nativePaths.agentsDirNote: Verified 2026-08-05 against docs.devin.ai/cli/subagents. Devin CLI reads subagent profiles from %APPDATA%/devin/agents on Windows (~/.config/devin/agents on macOS and Linux), each as agents/<name>/AGENT.md -- a directory per agent, not a flat file per agent. Path correct; absent only because AgentHub does not generate Devin subagents: registry/subagent-formats.json is scoped to four hosts and devin is not one of them.
nativePaths.hooksDirNote: Set to null 2026-08-05; previously claimed a directory at %APPDATA%/devin/hooks that does not exist as a concept. docs.devin.ai/cli/extensibility/hooks/overview documents NO user-level hooks directory: project hooks are a single file .devin/hooks.v1.json, and user-level hooks are configured as a 'hooks' key nested inside %APPDATA%/devin/config.json itself. Left as an explicit null rather than deleted, so the next person to notice that every other host has a hooks directory finds the answer instead of re-adding the wrong path.

nativePaths.hooksFileNote: Corrected 2026-08-05. Previously recorded as a directory ~/.codeium/windsurf/hooks, which does not exist and never did. docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/hooks (redirecting to docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/hooks after the merger) documents global hooks as a single FILE, hooks.json, merged with workspace .windsurf/hooks.json and system-level C:/ProgramData/Windsurf/hooks.json. The old value is exactly what this field's accountability rule exists to catch: a plausible directory name nobody had checked. Field renamed from hooksDir to hooksFile in the same change, because a field whose name says Dir while its value names a file is the identical quiet wrongness one layer along. Nothing consumes this field programmatically -- it is declarative, read only by the inventory sweep, which iterates fields generically.
nativePaths.workflowsDirNote: Corrected 2026-08-05. Previously recorded as ~/.codeium/windsurf/workflows, which does not exist. docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/workflows documents the global directory as global_workflows/*.md, available in every workspace and not committed; the project-scoped equivalent is .windsurf/workflows/*.md. Both this and hooksDir were wrong in the same host entry, which is why an absent path is not evidence of an unused feature.
